title: Learn QA
tagline: From exploratory checks to disciplined quality ownership
description: A three-level curriculum for QA engineers — learning to find defects early, design solid test cases, run regression with confidence, and partner with engineering on risk-based quality for web and API products.
prerequisites: Comfort using browsers and common desktop apps
Basic understanding of how websites and APIs work
Willingness to write clear bug reports and follow checklists

levels.title: QA Foundations
levels.goal: Comfortable exploring products, writing clear bugs, and executing basic test cases

topics.title: What QA owns
items: Shift-left and when to stop testing

topics.title: Bug reporting
items: Repro steps, expected vs. actual, and environment

topics.title: Test case design
items: Happy path, edge cases, and negative tests

topics.title: Exploratory testing
items: Note-taking that turns into actionable bugs

topics.title: Browser testing
items: DevTools console and network tab basics
Cross-browser smoke on Chrome, Safari, and Firefox

topics.title: API smoke with Postman
items: Saving a small collection for a feature

projects: Write and execute a test suite for a login + signup flow
File 10 well-structured bugs against a sample web app
Exploratory charter report for a checkout or booking flow
Postman collection covering CRUD on a public sample API

levels.title: Structured Quality Engineering
levels.goal: Plan releases, own regression, and test integrations with measurable coverage

topics.title: Regression & release support
items: Smoke, sanity, and full regression suites

topics.title: API depth
items: Auth headers, tokens, and role-based access

topics.title: Usability, a11y, and compatibility
items: Keyboard navigation and basic WCAG checks

projects: End-to-end test plan for a multi-step feature release
API regression suite (Postman) with auth and negative cases
Cross-browser matrix report with risk-ranked findings
Release readiness checklist used on a mock sprint release

levels.title: Quality Leadership
levels.goal: Define quality strategy, coach teams, and reduce escaped defects systematically

topics.title: Metrics that matter
items: Escape rate, reopen rate, and cycle time
Coverage as risk reduction, not vanity counts

topics.title: Process design
items: Definition of Done that includes test evidence

topics.title: Specialized testing
items: Security-minded checks (authZ, injection surfaces) at a QA level
Production monitoring signals that feed back into test design

topics.title: Automation partnership
items: What to automate vs. keep manual
Reviewing automation PRs for coverage gaps
Flake triage and CI gate ownership

projects: Quality strategy doc for a product area with metrics and gates
Post-incident RCA with preventive test additions
QA playbook (severity rubric, DoD, release checklist)
Automation ROI review: propose what to automate next quarter
